title: Salvianolic Acid B Reduces the Inflammation of Fat Grafts by Inhibiting the NF-Kb Signalling Pathway in Macrophages.
authors: Sun, Jia-Ming; Ho, Chia-Kang; Gao, Ya; Chong, Chio-Hou; Liu, Yang-Dan; Liu, Yu-Xin; Zheng, Dan-Ning; Zhang, Yi-Fan; Yu, Li
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹酚酸B通过抑制NF-κB信号通路改善脂肪移植炎症，核心为小分子-激酶互作与细胞实验，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Autologous fat grafting is a common method for soft tissue defect repair. However, the high absorption rate of transplanted fat is currently a bottleneck in the process. Excessive inflammation is one of the main reasons for poor fat transplantation. Salvianolic acid B (Sal-B) is a herbal medicine that shows promise for improving the effectiveness of fat transplantation. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to improve fat graft survival by injecting Sal-B into fat grafts locally. METHODS: In vivo, 0.2 mL of Coleman fat was transplanted into nude mice along with Sal-B. The grafts were evaluated by histologic analysis at 2, 4, and 12 weeks posttransplantation and by microcomputed tomography at 4 weeks posttransplantation. In vitro ribonucleic acid sequencing, cell proliferation assays, anti-inflammatory activity assays, molecular docking studies, and kinase activity assays were performed in RAW264.7 cells to detect the potential mechanism. RESULTS: Sal-B significantly improved fat graft survival and attenuated adipose tissue fibrosis and inflammation. Sal-B also inhibited the polarization of M1 macrophages in fat grafts. In vitro, Sal-B inhibited the proliferation and activation of inflammatory pathways in RAW264.7 cells. In addition, Sal-B had an inhibitory effect on NF-kappaB (nuclear factor kappa light polypeptide gene enhancer in B cells) signaling. This bioactivity of Sal-B may result from its selective binding to the kinase domain of the inhibitor of NF-kappaB kinase subunit beta. CONCLUSIONS: Sal-B could serve as a promising agent for improving the effect of fat transplantation by inhibiting the polarization of M1 macrophages through NF-kappaB signaling.
abstract_zh: 背景：自体脂肪移植是软组织缺损修复的常用方法。然而，移植脂肪的高吸收率目前是该过程中的瓶颈。过度炎症是导致脂肪移植效果不佳的主要原因之一。丹酚酸B（Salvianolic acid B, Sal-B）是一种草药，有望改善脂肪移植的效果。目的：本研究旨在通过将Sal-B局部注射到脂肪移植物中，以提高脂肪移植物的存活率。方法：在体内实验中，将0.2 mL Coleman脂肪与Sal-B一起移植到裸鼠体内。在移植后2、4和12周通过组织学分析评估移植物，并在移植后4周通过微型计算机断层扫描评估。在体外实验中，在RAW264.7细胞中进行核糖核酸测序、细胞增殖实验、抗炎活性实验、分子对接研究和激酶活性实验，以检测潜在机制。结果：Sal-B显著提高了脂肪移植物的存活率，并减轻了脂肪组织的纤维化和炎症。Sal-B还抑制了脂肪移植物中M1巨噬细胞的极化。在体外，Sal-B抑制了RAW264.7细胞的增殖和炎症通路的激活。此外，Sal-B对NF-κB（核因子κB轻链增强子激活B细胞）信号具有抑制作用。Sal-B的这种生物活性可能源于其选择性结合NF-κB激酶亚基β抑制剂的激酶结构域。结论：Sal-B可能通过NF-κB信号抑制M1巨噬细胞的极化，从而成为改善脂肪移植效果的有前景的药物。
